findings.source_quote: ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ γὰρ ἐκοιμήθησαν καὶ ἐν μεγάλῃ ἁγνείᾳ· μόνον δὲ τὴν σφραγῖδα ταύτην οὐκ εἶχον.
findings.english_quote: Retain each group’s stated responsibility, possibility or exclusion of repentance, and the life/death consequences.
findings.issue: The per-unit theological metadata identifies differentiated repentance as a feature of this passage, although no clause here states a possibility, condition, or exclusion of repentance. The passage instead distinguishes the groups through their prior righteousness and purity, possession of the seal, and descent and ascent as dead or living. This is an unsupported characterization of the selected source, even though the reader text does not insert repentance.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the repentance-specific metadata with a description of this unit’s actual distinctions: water and seal, the necessity and unless condition, proclamation to those who died earlier, and the differing life/death states. Review the replacement separately.

findings.source_quote: κοιμηθέντες ἐν δυνάμει καὶ πίστει τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ
findings.english_quote: After falling asleep in his power and faith
findings.issue: The possessive wording makes both power and faith sound like attributes possessed by the Son. In particular, “his faith” sharpens the Greek genitive into the Son’s own faith, rather than preserving the possible relationship of the deceased people’s faith to the Son. The standard’s “faith of the Son of God” leaves that relationship more open. No theological decision or note discloses the simplified edition’s narrowing.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider restoring “after falling asleep in the power and faith of the Son of God.” If an explicitly interpretive rendering is preferred, document the chosen relationship and preserve the relevant alternative in a note. Neither proposal should be accepted without fresh review.

findings.source_quote: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ συνανέβησαν μετ᾿ αὐτῶν καὶ συνηρμόσθησαν εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου, καὶ ἀλατόμητοι συνῳκοδομήθησαν· ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ γὰρ ἐκοιμήθησαν καὶ ἐν μεγάλῃ ἁγνείᾳ·
findings.english_quote: They came up together and were fitted into the building of the tower. They were built in without being hewn. They had fallen asleep in righteousness and great purity.
findings.issue: The simplification drops both explicit explanatory links: “for this reason” connects their ascent and incorporation to the preceding account, and “for” explains their incorporation without hewing by their prior righteousness and purity. It also loses the joint-building sense of συνῳκοδομήθησαν by reducing it to “built in.” These are source relationships, not merely sentence-length preferences.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “That is why they also came up with them and were fitted into the building of the tower. They were built together without being hewn, because they had fallen asleep in righteousness and great purity.” Review this proposed wording against the source before adopting it.

findings.source_quote: ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ γὰρ ἐκοιμήθησαν καὶ ἐν μεγάλῃ ἁγνείᾳ· μόνον δὲ τὴν σφραγῖδα ταύτην οὐκ εἶχον.
findings.english_quote: Retain conditional repentance, all names and stone counts, water/seal and life/death imagery; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims to retain conditional repentance, but this unit contains no repentance expression or repentance condition. The shared theological metadata likewise presents differentiated repentance as a feature of the unit. These descriptions import a topic from elsewhere rather than accurately documenting this passage.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the conditional-repentance claim and revise the theological metadata to describe the actual distinctions concerning the seal, prior righteousness and purity, and life/death states. Retain the source’s water-related necessity and unless condition without relabeling them as repentance conditions. Review the revised metadata separately.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard reader text covers the selected working source faithfully, but its repentance metadata mischaracterizes this unit. The simplified edition additionally loses explicit causal and joint-building relationships and narrows the faith expression without disclosure. Both retain the difficult necessity, negation, seal-as-water assertion, and proclamation to those who died earlier. The textual notes appropriately distinguish working-edition supplements and reported transmission alternatives; this assessment does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify an exhaustive collation. Proposed corrections require fresh review.
